about: Root motion the controller should reproduce, per clip. forward_m / left_m / turn_left_deg are per frame from the clip's first frame; speed_mps and turn_deg are the totals.

pistol.about: The pistol node shows from the draw's show_frame and hides after the holster's hide_after_frame (frames counted from 1). The bolt leaves the muzzle node on the fire clip's shot_frame.

aim.about: Aim offsets for the pistol: held upper-body poses on a pitch x yaw grid (degrees; pitch up +, yaw toward the droid's left +), each the exact barrel direction. Blend the four around the wanted (pitch, yaw) bilinearly, then lay the result on the playing pistol clip as an additive offset against the reference pose (frame 1 of reference_clip), per bone in its parent's space: rotation = current * ref^-1 * offset; position += offset - ref. Only the bones listed move; hips and legs are left to the leg clip.

eyes.note: set base colour and emissive of eye_glow to the mood colour; keep emission on in every mood

ragdoll.about: Ragdoll for droid_full_deform.glb, built by build_ragdoll.py. One rigid body per entry in `bodies`, driving `bone`; `passengers` are deform bones that just ride along (they keep their last local pose).
ragdoll.frames: Every position/rotation is in the body's bone-local frame as the GLB has it (origin at the bone's head, Y along the bone, X = the bend axis). A body's global transform IS its bone's global transform (what Fyrox's Ragdoll node syncs). Quaternions are [x, y, z, w]. rest_gltf = the bone's bind pose in glTF model space (Y up, droid facing +Z), at model scale 1.
ragdoll.scale: Lengths are at model scale 1. The game draws the droid at avatar SCALE (0.85): multiply every position, radius and half-extent by it, and masses by SCALE^3 if the density should stay the same.
ragdoll.joints: Ball joints (Fyrox BallJoint). Build them with the droid in its bind pose (nodes as loaded), each joint node at the body's own bone frame (= parent body * frame_in_parent), so Fyrox's auto-computed local frames equal frame_in_parent / frame_in_body. Then turn auto-rebinding off. limits_deg are Rapier angular limits on the joint's x/y/z (enable all three); rest pose = 0 on every axis.
ragdoll.collisions: Each body is alone in its collision_bit. Collider InteractionGroups: memberships = 1 << bit, filter = everything except the bits of the bodies in `ignores` (jointed neighbours, and pairs that touch in some clip). The droid's own character capsule must stop colliding with the limbs while the ragdoll is active (make it a sensor or take it out of the limbs' filter).

physics.note: joint damping = Joint::set_motor_resistive_torque_as_ball(0, joint_max_torque, joint_damping) on every joint. solver_iterations is the scene's IntegrationParameters::num_solver_iterations (Fyrox default 4): with 4 the joints stretch more on impact and the shoulders overshoot their limits by 10-40 deg; with 8 by under 5. Values are the ones ragdoll_sim was tuned with.

fyrox: Spawn the model; before it animates, for each body in order: a RigidBody as a child of one Ragdoll node that has the scene root's transform (not the scaled model), at the bone's global transform, its colliders as children with density = density_kg_m3 (that gives mass_kg AND the inertia; don't use the body's additional mass with density-0 colliders: Rapier scales the inertia from the colliders, so the limbs could not turn).
For each body with a joint: a Joint node at the body's global transform, body1 = parent body, body2 = this body, BallJoint with limits_deg in radians, contacts off, auto-rebinding off.
Ragdoll root_limb = pelvis, children as in `parent`; is_active false while animated (the bodies then follow the bones kinematically).

To fall: stop the animation player's writes to the body bones, set is_active true, set character_rigid_body (its velocity is handed to the limbs), apply the hit as an impulse on the body that was hit.
